summary: The seven requested Drizzle columns, their focused runtime boundaries, ST normalization, open ModelId parser, and sentinel placement are coherent and pass focused verification. The completion claim is nevertheless false because one production castId<ProviderId> bypass remains in the credentials producer.

findings.title: The credentials writer still brands provider identity with castId
evidence: packages/server/src/domain/credentials/verbs/add.ts:30-33 first asks a boolean providerKnown predicate, then creates ProviderId with castId<ProviderId>(params.provider).

packages/server/src/entry/compose/services.ts:390-395 binds providerKnown to registry.get(id) !== undefined, so the current composition validates membership, but the branded registry row is discarded and the writer still uses the unchecked cast primitive.
Actual ast-grep: pnpm exec ast-grep run --lang ts --pattern 'castId<ProviderId>($A)' packages --inspect=summary returned exactly this production hit after scanning 2,631 TypeScript files.
The matching ModelId scan returned zero after the same 2,631-file scan.
findings.impact: The stated no-bypass invariant is not true, and the CredentialContext contract can brand any string if providerKnown is ever misbound or weakened. This is especially material because the value is persisted and used in credential AAD.
findings.recommendedRepair: Replace the boolean predicate plus cast with an operation that returns the registered ProviderDef/ProviderId and use that row's branded id, matching connection/verbs/connections.ts:35-39 and 135-149. Add a type or behavior pin so the credentials producer cannot recover ProviderId from a boolean check plus cast.
